title: What is known about 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open; every sub-round is now proved in Lean, small gaps included. One pass machine (a left sweep, then a right sweep in three phases with nine local moves) gives every sub-round, regular or not, for every size and every tape, and the only way it halts is the carry meeting 011 in phase A. With it, the counter in closed form and the list read as the binary expansion of the time it has left, the run from blank tape is proved in Lean to rebuild 40 (a single block of 3,483 cells, more than 10349 steps). What is left is arithmetic: whether the counters the run produces ever lead the carry to a halting 011. The hybrid run passes 986 rebuilds, more than 1031,896 steps, without a halt.

It can halt from tapes of its own shape. A single block of 3k cells that meets the counter exactly at the start of a round halts (k = 3 to 9, direct simulation). Whether the run from blank tape ever produces such a coincidence is the open question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 189 cells have been visited and 86 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in C on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: No halt in 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps; three rebuilds
claims.text: Direct simulation for 3·10<sup>10</sup> steps. At the moments the head is in C on the first 0 right of everything written the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s; the last block grows by 4 per round; in walking phases the rounds satisfy T′ = 2T + 4 exactly. Rebuilds of the list at steps 72,083, 11,004,261 and 22,558,329,283 (the table).

claims.title: Between rebuilds: a binary counter that applies one list operation per tick
claims.text: At the moments the head is in C on a 0 just right of a 1, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (the interior), a last block l, and to the right of the head a zone of single 1s. Call it regular if the first block is a multiple of 3, the other interior blocks are 2 mod 3, l is 1 mod 4, and the gaps of the zone are 0 mod 4 (the first, counted from the head) and 3 mod 4 (the others). From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) a regular configuration changes in two independent ways. The interior takes one step W: (..., x, 3a + 2) becomes (..., x + 3, 2, ..., 2) with a blocks of 2. The last block and the zone are a binary counter: with segments s<sub>1</sub> = g<sub>1</sub>, s<sub>i</sub> = g<sub>i</sub> + 1, a last block l ≥ 5 becomes a new first segment l − 1 and l = 1; with l = 1 the n leading segments equal to 4 are removed, the next segment loses 4 cells (blank tape supplies them if there is none) and l = 4n + 5. So l plus the segments is 4m + 1 for 2<sup>m</sup> sub-rounds (one round, what earlier notes called the fast counter), then m grows by 1. Checked against the machine one sub-round at a time: of the 300,000 sub-rounds after step 2,918 (12.6 million steps) the 299,954 regular ones all follow this; the other 46 are the transients of the first two rebuilds. The rules are now proved in Lean for all sizes (the claims below); this check of the machine stays as a test.

claims.title: The binary expansion, checked on the machine
claims.text: With digits ai = (bi − 2)/3, W removes the last digit a, adds 1 to the digit before it and appends a zeros; the sum of all digits plus their number never changes. A tail (..., q, a) becomes (..., q + a + 1) after exactly 2a steps, so an interior with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T = Σi 2ai + ... + ak + k − i steps of W: the positions of the 1s in the binary expansion of T are the partial sums of the list read from the right. Checked on the machine: the model predicts single blocks at sub-rounds 1,616 and 261,907 of that run and both are there; W steps and counter steps taken many at once agree with the machine in 28 test jumps; and after the third rebuild the lists at seven ends of rounds, up to step 2.8·1010, are those of a direct run of the machine (3 2^25 14 2 8 2 14 | 85 at step 22,558,329,286, ..., 3 2^12 20 2^6 14 2 8 2 14 | 109 at step 28,107,393,382).

claims.title: Every sub-round of the regular kind, for all sizes
claims.text: Five machine rules, each for every value of its parameters and every tape further out: glong (last interior block 3a + 2, last block b + 2: W on the interior, the last block becomes 1 and a new zone gap of b + 1), gshort (last block 1: the carry removes the leading gaps of 3, takes 4 cells from the next gap, which has at least 4, and sets the last block to 4n + 5), gzero (the carry meets two 1s side by side before a gap of at least 2: last block 4n + 4), and the two rebuild sub-rounds below. Put together (subround): at the moments the head is in C on a 0 right of a 1, a configuration 1^(3q) 0 [digits] 0 1^l C> [gaps] with at least one digit goes in one sub-round to W of its digits and one step gstep of the counter, which is defined for every last block and every zone except at the small gaps (a carry meeting a gap of 1 or 2 cells, or two 1s side by side before a gap of 0 or 1). The rules are proved by rfl steps, the crossing lemmas and omega; the earlier observation that W and the counter do not influence each other is now a theorem.

claims.title: The list is the binary expansion of the time it has left
claims.text: With T(x :: r) = 2^x (1 + 2 T(r)) on the digits listed nearest the head first, W lowers T by exactly 1 and keeps the first block plus the digits plus their number (T_W, mass_W). So from any configuration of this shape the machine reaches the single block of 3 · mass cells after exactly T sub-rounds, the counter advanced T times, if the counter meets no small gap on the way (collapse; advance for fewer sub-rounds). A regular counter (last block 1 mod 4, every gap 3 mod 4: the binary counter of the picture) never meets one (regular_total), so from a regular configuration the collapse always happens, without a halt (collapse_regular).

claims.title: The rebuild sub-round, and why single blocks grow
claims.text: A single block of 3(k + 1) cells with last block b + 5 becomes 3 2^k with last block 5 and a new zone gap of b cells in front (rebuild, rule single); with last block 1 and a first gap of at least 2 it becomes 3 2^k with last block 4 and the first gap 2 shorter (rebuild_one, rule singleone). The digits of 3 2^k give T = 2k − 1 and mass k + 1, so if the counter meets no small gap the single block comes back with the same 3(k + 1) cells after 2k sub-rounds (rebuild_cycle). The single blocks of the run grow (36, 57, 90, ...) only because small gaps move cells of the counter into the list; the new gap a rebuild makes (b, a multiple of 4 when the last block is 1 mod 4) is where the first small gap comes from.

claims.title: The run from blank tape through the first rebuild, to step 71,355
claims.text: The kernel evaluates the first 2,918 steps (to 3 2 8 5 14 | 9) and the counter gstep; the rest is the rules above: 1,616 sub-rounds to the single block of 36 cells (first_single), the rebuild sub-round (first_rebuild, step 70,871: 3 2^11 | 5), and 13 more sub-rounds to step 71,355, where the carry meets a gap of 2 cells, the first sub-round of the run the rules do not cover (first_uncovered).

claims.title: Every sub-round, small gaps included: the pass machine
claims.text: At every moment (the head in C on a 0, a last block l on its left, then any blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, and on its right any zone of gaps) the next sub-round is the same two sweeps. The left sweep (start) erases the last block, moves the block before it one cell to the right and adds 3 cells to the block before that. The right sweep reads the tape in one of three phases A, E, C (the machine states) with an open block, the 1s just left of the head. On a 1, A writes 0 (the open block closes, an empty one opens) and E and C keep it; the phase goes A, E, C, A. On a 0: C after a non-empty open block is the next moment (the open block is the new last block); C or E next to an empty open block fill two cells; E after an open block, and A on 010, move the open block one cell right, add 3 to the block before it and start again in A; A on 000 writes 111 and goes on in C; A on 001 writes 101 (the open block closes at the middle cell); A on 011 halts. Each move is a machine rule proved for every size (lean/Pass.lean, generated by py/gen_pass.py); pstep puts them into one total function, and sub_moment and sub_halt prove that a sub-round it computes is a run of the machine with exactly its number of steps, and that a halt it finds is a halt of the machine. So the halts of the machine are exactly the carries that meet 011 in phase A. W on the list and the binary counter (the rules above) are the cases where the right sweep only meets blocks 2 mod 3 and gaps 3 mod 4; the small gaps are the moves A on 001 and 010, which move cells of the counter into the list.

claims.title: The run from blank tape through two transients, to the third single block
claims.text: From step 71,355 (where the first small gap was the end of the proved run) the kernel evaluates the pass machine: 7 sub-rounds of the first transient to the regular configuration 3 2^6 11 5^2 2^2 5 | 5 with zone gaps 4 7 3 (first_transient); collapse, with the counter evaluated by the kernel (260,270 counter steps), gives the second single block, 57 cells (second_single); rebuild and 24 more sub-rounds of the pass machine give 3 2^13 11 5^2 2^2 5 2^2 5 | 9, a regular configuration (second_transient); and collapse_regular the third single block, 90 cells, 536,840,942 sub-rounds later, with a regular counter (third_single). Direct simulation puts that block at step 22,558,329,283; the Lean proof does not evaluate any machine step past step 2,918, and the counter after the third block is left existential (it needs the counter in closed form).

claims.title: The run from blank tape to rebuild 40
claims.text: Two lemmas make the counter and the list cheap for the kernel at any size. Scaling (giter_scale): with 4j more cells in the last block, one step of the counter takes exactly 2j steps, so gfast advances the counter by N steps in about two jumps per binary digit of N (gfast_sound). Part of a collapse (advance_to): W lowers the time left T by one and keeps the mass, and T is one to one (the list is the binary expansion of T), so after M sub-rounds the digits are the only list D′ with T(D′) + M = T(D); no step of W is evaluated. From the third single block the run is then a chain of 454 segments (lean/Chain.lean, generated by py/gen_chain.py 40): 227 advances, W and the counter for as many sub-rounds as the counter makes before it meets a small gap of the zone (up to about 21,160 at once), and 227 passes, 1 to 3 sub-rounds of the pass machine evaluated by the kernel where the counter is stuck (a small gap, or a single block and its rebuild). single_40: the run from blank tape reaches the single block of rebuild 40, 3,483 cells, after more than 21,160 sub-rounds (so more than 10349 machine steps), and does not halt before it. The single blocks of rebuilds 4 to 40 are those of the hybrid run of py/model.py.

claims.title: What the regular rules leave, and the pass machine against the run
claims.text: Before the pass machine: the hybrid run of py/model.py through 243 rebuilds with every directly simulated sub-round checked against the regular rules (c/rules_check.c): of 70,055 sub-rounds simulated directly in the transients, 67,154 follow a regular rule with its exact step count and none differs; 2,901 are not covered, 1,584 where the carry meets a small gap and 1,317 where cells the small gaps moved into the list leave a last block that is not 2 mod 3. The pass machine covers all of them. Its Python mirror py/passm.py, move for move the Lean function, agrees with the machine on 30,000 random tapes (configuration, step count and halts) and, in the hybrid run through 243 rebuilds, gives for every one of the 24,034 stretches the run simulates cell by cell (the transients and the sub-rounds where the counter reaches an irregular gap; 363,515,147 machine steps) exactly the configuration and step count of c/trans.c.

claims.title: Tapes of the same shape that halt
claims.text: A rebuild starts when the interior is a single block. The tape 1<sup>3k</sup> 0 1<sup>4k−3</sup> with the head in C on the 0 right of it, a single block of 3k cells meeting the counter exactly at the start of round k − 1, halts for every k from 3 to 9 (after 311, 659, 1,343, 2,699, 5,399, 10,787 and 21,551 steps; direct simulation). So no property of the shape alone can show that the machine never halts: it depends on which single blocks and counter values the run from blank tape produces.

claims.title: 986 rebuilds without a halt
claims.text: A run that takes the regular sub-rounds by arithmetic (any number at once, with the two rules above) and gives everything else to the machine itself, cell by cell: the transient after each single block, and the sub-rounds where the counter reaches an irregular gap of the zone. It passes 986 rebuilds; by then the counter has made more than 2105,958 sub-rounds, so the machine more than 1031,896 steps, and the single block has 317,877 cells. A halt could only be found by the direct part and none was. The sub-rounds the arithmetic part takes are of the kinds proved in Lean for all sizes (W and the regular counter); the direct part is now covered by the pass machine as well (proved for every sub-round); what rests on Python is the arithmetic that takes many regular sub-rounds at once (applyW, enc/dec); through rebuild 40 that arithmetic is now proved too (above). The small gaps never hold the counter for long: in the segments of py/gen_chain.py through rebuild 200 (single block 54,075 cells), each of the 1,410 places where the counter is stuck is cleared by 1, 2 or 3 sub-rounds of the pass machine (403, 933 and 74 times).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Every sub-round is proved, with its exact step count, and the only halting move is a carry that meets 011 in phase A (a gap of one cell followed by two 1s side by side). Tapes of the same shape do halt that way (the halting family above ends with the zone ... 3 3 1 0). So the question is arithmetic: whether the single blocks and counters that this run produces ever lead a carry to such a place. The halting family needs the single block to arrive exactly when a round of the counter starts, a coincidence of two binary numbers that the run has avoided so far. In Lean the run is proved to rebuild 40 (more than 10349 steps); each further rebuild costs the kernel a few more segments, so the proved run can be pushed further, but a proof for all rebuilds needs a rule for the counter at the moment the single block arrives.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Between its rebuilds this machine is a binary counter that applies one small operation to a list of blocks at every tick, and the list is, read in binary, the time left until the next rebuild. Every step of this, the irregular sub-rounds after each rebuild included, is one simple sweep machine, now proved in Lean for every size. This page runs the machine, lets you step the list, the counter and the sweep machine, and lists what is known.

facts.text: One pass machine, proved in Lean for all sizes, small gaps included.
The run from blank tape to the single block of rebuild 40 (3,483 cells, more than 10<sup>349</sup> steps), proved.
Tapes of the same shape that halt.

sections.heading: A binary counter that rewrites a list
html: Stop the machine each time the head is in state C on a 0 just right of a 1. The tape is then a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, a last block, and right of the head a zone of single 1s. From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) two things happen, and they do not influence each other.

The list takes one step. Its last block, of 3a + 2 cells, gives 3 cells to the block on its left and falls apart into a blocks of 2: x, 3a+2 becomes x+3, 2, ..., 2. Counting a block of 3a + 2 as the digit a: the last digit a is removed, the digit before it grows by 1, and a zeros are appended.

The counter ticks. The last block and the zone hold a binary counter. A round is 2m sub-rounds in which they fill 4m + 1 cells; then the last block is 4m + 5 cells and round m + 1 starts. This is why each round takes twice as long as the one before.

The list gets shorter in the end, and how long that takes can be read off it: a list with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T steps, where T has a binary 1 at the positions ak, ak + ak−1 + 1, ak + ak−1 + ak−2 + 2, and so on. The list is the time it has left, written in binary. Try it:

The start values are the tape at step 2,918 from blank tape (last block 9, so round 2). All of this was first read off the run and checked against the machine; it is now proved in Lean for every size: one sub-round is W on the list and one step of the counter (subround), and W lowers T by exactly one (T_W), so the single block comes after exactly T sub-rounds (collapse).

Rebuilds. When a single block of 3(k + 1) cells is left, one sub-round cuts it into 3 2^k (proved), and the last block leaves a new gap in the zone. On its own that would bring back the same single block after 2k sub-rounds. What makes the list longer is a cascade of small gaps: when the counter's carry reaches the new gap after it has shrunk to 1 or 2 cells, cells of the counter move into the list. These few dozen sub-rounds per rebuild (the transient) are not W and the counter, but they are the same sweep machine (next section), proved for every size. The first rebuilds:

sections.heading: One sweep machine, small gaps included
html: W on the list and the counter are not the whole story: after each rebuild come sub-rounds where the counter meets a gap of 1 or 2 cells and cells of the counter move into the list. All sub-rounds, these included, are one and the same procedure, now proved in Lean for every size and every tape (lean/General.lean).

The left sweep. The head runs left, erases the last block, moves the block before it one cell to the right and adds 3 cells to the block before that. Then it turns right in state A, in front of the moved block.

The right sweep reads the tape in one of three phases A, E, C, with an open block: the 1s just left of the head. On a 1, A writes 0 (the open block closes) and E and C keep the 1; the phase goes A, E, C, A, so a block of 3a + 2 ones becomes (011)^a 01: that is W. On a 0:

• C after a non-empty open block: the sub-round is over, the open block is the new last block;
  • C or E next to an empty open block: the two cells become 11;
  • E after an open block, or A on 010: the open block moves one cell to the right, the block before it grows by 3, and A starts again in front of the moved block;
  • A on 000: 111, then C (the counter's carry through a gap of 3: 0001 becomes 1111);
  • A on 001: 101, the open block closes at the middle cell and becomes a block of the list (a small gap of 2);
  • A on 011: the machine halts. This is the only way it can halt.

Step it below. The presets are the run at step 71,355 (the first small gap after the first rebuild), the second rebuild, and a tape of the halting family (k = 4). Blocks are written from the left, the last one being the last block; the first zone gap counts the head's cell.
presets:

With this the kernel evaluates every stretch where the counter is stuck (never more than 3 sub-rounds through rebuild 200), the rest is W and the counter taken many sub-rounds at once (proved: with 4j more cells in the last block one counter step takes 2j, and the list after M sub-rounds is the one whose time left is M less), and the run from blank tape is proved to rebuild 40. The halting tapes reach the zone 4 3 ... 3 1 0 (gaps of 3, then a gap of one cell, then two 1s side by side) when the carry arrives in phase A; the run from blank tape has never let that happen.

 if(ph==='C'){if(hd(lb)===0)return {t:'next',m:'C on 0 next to 0: 11',s:[[hd(t)+2].concat(t.slice(1)),'C',0,rd(us)],n:3};
  return {t:'done',m:'C on 0 after the open block: the next moment',bs:t,l:hd(lb),us:rd(us),n:0};}
 if(ph==='E'){if(hd(lb)===0)return {t:'next',m:'E on 0 next to 0: 11',s:[[hd(t)+2].concat(t.slice(1)),'C',0,rd(us)],n:5};
  return {t:'next',m:'E on 0: the open block ('+hd(lb)+') moves right, the block before it +3',s:[[hd(t)+3].concat(t.slice(1)),'A',hd(lb)-1,rd(us)],n:3*(hd(lb)-1)+9};}
 if(!us.length||us[0]>=3)return {t:'next',m:'A on 000: 111',s:[[hd(lb)+3].concat(lb.slice(1)),'C',0,us.length?[us[0]-3].concat(us.slice(1)):[]],n:5};
 if(us[0]===2)return {t:'next',m:'A on 001: 101, a block of '+(hd(lb)+1)+' moves into the list',s:[[1,hd(lb)+1].concat(lb.slice(1)),'A',0,us.slice(1)],n:3};
 if(us.length>1&&us[1]===0)return {t:'halt',m:'A on 011: HALT'};
 return {t:'next',m:'A on 010: the open block ('+hd(lb)+') moves right, the block before it +3',s:[[hd(t)+3].concat(t.slice(1)),'A',hd(lb)+1,rd(us.slice(1))],n:3*hd(lb)+12};}
function sub(bs,l,us,log){
 var p=bs[0],rest=bs.slice(1);var s=[[hd(rest)+3].concat(rest.slice(1)),'A',p,[l-1].concat(us)];var n=(l-1)+3*(p-1)+15;
 log.push('left sweep: last block '+l+' erased, block '+p+' moves right, the block before it +3');
 for(var i=0;i<100000;i++){var r=pstep(s[0],s[1],s[2],s[3]);if(r.m)log.push(r.m);
  if(r.t==='next'){s=r.s;n+=r.n;}else if(r.t==='done'){return {bs:r.bs,l:r.l,us:r.us,n:n+r.n};}else return null;}
 return null;}
function rle(I){var o=[],c=0;for(var i=0;i<I.length;i++){if(i+1<I.length&&I[i+1]===I[i]){c++;continue;}o.push(c?I[i]+'^'+(c+1):''+I[i]);c=0;}return o.join(' ');}
function expand(s){var o=[];s.trim().split(/\s+/).forEach(function(w){if(!w)return;var m=w.split('^');var v=parseInt(m[0]),c=m.length>1?parseInt(m[1]):1;for(var i=0;i<c;i++)o.push(v);});return o;}
var st=null,steps=0,count=0;
function cur(){return rle(st.bs.slice().reverse())+' | '+st.l+' | '+(st.us.length?[st.us[0]+1].concat(st.us.slice(1)).join(' '):'(blank)');}
function set(){var b=expand(document.getElementById('pw-b').value);var g=expand(document.getElementById('pw-g').value);
 st={bs:b.slice(0,-1).reverse(),l:b[b.length-1],us:g.length?[g[0]-1].concat(g.slice(1)):[]};steps=0;count=0;
 document.getElementById('pw-out').textContent='blocks | last block | zone gaps (the first counts the head cell)\n'+cur();}
function go(N,showmoves){if(!st)set();var out=document.getElementById('pw-out');var txt=out.textContent;
 for(var i=0;i<N;i++){var log=[];var r=sub(st.bs,st.l,st.us,log);
  if(!r){txt+='\n'+(showmoves?'  '+log.join('\n  ')+'\n':'')+'the machine halts in this sub-round (the carry met 011 in phase A)';st=null;break;}
  st=r;steps+=r.n;count++;txt+='\n'+(showmoves?'  '+log.join('\n  ')+'\n':'')+'sub-round '+count+' ('+r.n+' steps, '+steps+' in all): '+cur();}
 out.textContent=txt;}
function preset(b,g){document.getElementById('pw-b').value=b;document.getElementById('pw-g').value=g;set();}
document.getElementById('pw-set').onclick=set;
document.getElementById('pw-1').onclick=function(){go(1,true);};
document.getElementById('pw-10').onclick=function(){go(10,false);};
document.getElementById('pw-p1').onclick=function(){preset('3 2^6 8 5 1','4 3 2 5 7 11 3');};
document.getElementById('pw-p2').onclick=function(){preset('3 2^18 5','5 11 3 3 15 3 3 3 3 3 3');};
document.getElementById('pw-p3').onclick=function(){preset('12 13','');};
set();})();
</script>

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1. In a sub-round between rebuilds that does not happen (proved). In the irregular stretch after a single block it can: the tape 1^(3k) 0 1^(4k−3) C>0, a single block of 3k cells arriving exactly when round k − 1 of the counter starts, halts for k = 3, ..., 9 (311, 659, 1,343, ... steps; each about twice the one before).

So the question is one about two binary numbers: the time T the list needs, which is written in the list itself, and the state of the counter. The run from blank tape has passed 986 rebuilds, more than 1031,896 steps, without a halt. The first 40 rebuilds are proved in Lean. Nothing proved says it stays that way: each rebuild is checked separately, and there is no rule yet for where the counter stands when the single block arrives.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).
After 109 steps the tape spans 189 cells (10 left of the start, 174 right), with a density of 1s of 0.455.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

sidesteptape
right715,604,2671^3 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^11 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^2 0 1^2 0 1^5 0 1^5 0 1^5 0 1^94 A>0
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: two-level block counter (fast tail, walker in a list of 2s, rebuilds)
summary: Binary counter applying one list operation W per tick; every sub-round (small gaps included) is one pass machine proved in Lean for all sizes, whose only halting move is the carry meeting 011; the run is proved to rebuild 40 (more than 10^349 steps); no halt in 986 rebuilds (more than 10^31,896 steps); tapes of the same shape halt; open.
